title: Anthropic secretly adds watermarks to Claude's output: Reddit erupts in controversy, with some users criticizing digital tattoos

content_html:
Anthropic has recently decided to add watermarks to the generated content of Claude, which means embedding invisible codes in the text produced by the chatbot to indicate that the content was generated by AI. This policy is aimed at meeting the transparency requirements of the EU AI Act, which mandates tech companies to mark AI-generated or edited content with computer-readable identifiers. While regulators may be satisfied, some AI users are clearly not happy, and discussions have already heated up on Reddit.

One of the most heated posts came from user visionode, whose account has been active for less than three weeks. He refers to this watermark system as a "strict conspiracy" designed to make innocent chatbot users victims. His core argument is that experts who are familiar with Claude can rewrite or use other AI services to hide their traces, while ordinary users are left vulnerable.

The "Digital Tattoo" Debate: Who Are the Real Victims?

visionode paints a picture of "victims": "Who will get caught? You - the student who asked Claude to reorganize text; the journalist who used AI to summarize 200 pages of interviews; the writer who asked AI for synonyms. These people will all end up with a digital tattoo on their forehead." However, these examples were quickly refuted: if a journalist only uses AI to summarize material, the watermark would not have a real impact unless he copies the AI summary directly into his article; a student who copies AI-revised paragraphs into a paper already violates academic ethics. Other users did not support his anger, with some leaving a comment like "look at this guy" and others advising him to "take a deep breath."

Another critic called the watermark "unethical" and "disgusting," emphasizing that he provided instructions, background information, and numerous revisions during his use of Claude, asking, "Claude is just a tool, what credit is it taking?" However, opponents responded that the watermark is not about taking credit but about traceability in scenarios where AI-generated content poses risks. Some users also raised deeper concerns: since cutting-edge AI models are trained on others' works, adding watermarks to AI-generated content carries a "frighteningly ironic" meaning. Nonetheless, overall, most users still support the watermark system, with one user's summary being particularly representative: "The only reason not to want such a mechanism is if you want to lie to others."

content_html_zh:
Anthropic 最近决定在 Claude 生成的内容中添加水印，这意味着在聊天机器人生成的文本中嵌入隐形代码，以表明该内容是由 AI 生成的。 该政策旨在满足欧盟人工智能法案的透明度要求，该法案要求科技公司使用计算机可读标识符来标记人工智能生成或编辑的内容。 虽然监管机构可能会感到满意，但一些人工智能用户显然并不高兴，Reddit 上的讨论已经升温。

最热门的帖子之一来自用户Visionode，其帐户活跃时间还不到三周。 他将这个水印系统称为“严格的阴谋”，旨在使无辜的聊天机器人用户成为受害者。 他的核心论点是，熟悉克劳德的专家可以重写或使用其他人工智能服务来隐藏他们的痕迹，而普通用户则容易受到攻击。

“数字纹身”争论：谁是真正的受害者？

Visionode描绘了一幅“受害者”的画面：“谁会被抓住？ 你——那个要求克劳德重新组织文本的学生；使用人工智能总结200页采访的记者；向人工智能询问同义词的作家。 这些人的额头上都会有数字纹身。” 然而，这些例子很快就被反驳了：如果记者只使用人工智能来总结素材，那么水印不会产生真正的影响，除非他将人工智能摘要直接复制到文章中；一名学生将人工智能修改过的段落复制到论文中已经违反了学术道德。 其他用户并不支持他的愤怒，一些人留下了“看看这个家伙”之类的评论，还有一些人建议他“深呼吸”。

另一位评论家称该水印“不道德”和“令人厌恶”，强调他在使用克劳德期间提供了说明、背景信息和多次修改，并问道：“克劳德只是一个工具，它有什么功劳？” 然而，反对者回应称，水印并不是为了抢功劳，而是为了在人工智能生成的内容带来风险的情况下进行追溯。 一些用户还提出了更深层次的担忧：由于最前沿的人工智能模型是在别人的作品上训练的，因此在人工智能生成的内容中添加水印带有“令人恐惧的讽刺”意义。 尽管如此，总体而言，大多数用户仍然支持水印系统，其中一位用户的总结尤其具有代表性：“不想要这种机制的唯一原因是如果你想对别人撒谎。”
